elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 10.14 covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; there is no commercial general liability limit anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit appears; Section 10.14 names only E&O ($1,000,000) and cyber/privacy ($2,000,000).

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 sets E&O at 'not less than $1,000,000', which is below the preferred USD 2,000,000 floor.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cellco as Servicer/Custodian handles Obligor account, payment and Receivable File data, so the condition applies, but the inserted cyber and privacy limit is only $2,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation covenant appears in Section 10.14 or elsewhere; the only other 'insurance' references are Obligor premium charges billed to accounts (p0095) and FDIC deposit insurance.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery or evidence-on-request mechanic.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 'The Servicer will maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $1,000,000' — an affirmative, unconditional covenant at the required floor in the agreement's dollar currency.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: '...and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000' — express cyber/privacy line at the required floor.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: both the E&O $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy $2,000,000 limits are stated as unconditional 'will maintain' covenants in new Section 10.14, with no undefined trigger and nothing merely promised in the margin comment.

Preferred level is not reached on five of six elements (no CGL 1M/2M, E&O only 1M rather than 2M, cyber only 2M rather than 5M, no workers' compensation, no certificates on request); the drafter correctly targeted fallback only, so this is not a defect in the chosen level.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a two-limb sentence with no model-language extras — no 'at its own expense', no term-plus-one-year survival tail, no certificate procedure, no CGL or workers' compensation add-ons beyond the fallback checklist. For a missing clause, wholly new wording is permissible.

Intent is preserved: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased. The two cited paragraphs (Obligor insurance premium charges at p0095 and the compliance language at p0439) are reproduced unchanged, and no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is disturbed.

Drafting note (not a failure of the fallback checklist): the covenant binds 'the Servicer' only, while Cellco also acts as Marketing Agent and Custodian and holds Receivable Files in the custodial capacity. If you want the cover to follow the data in every capacity, change the subject to 'Cellco, in each of its capacities under this Agreement'. Also confirm that Section 10.14 is the next unused number in Article X so the insertion does not collide with an existing section.
